title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: Live Logcat streaming with stacktrace deeplinks
summary: Adds a built-in Logcat panel with real-time ADB streaming, clickable stacktrace deeplinks, and automatic start on Android Run.

highlights.title: Built-in Logcat Panel
highlights.description: Stream logcat output from any connected Android device in a dedicated VS Code panel, with pause, resume, clear, and export controls. No Android Studio or terminal tab required.

highlights.title: Stacktrace Deeplinks
highlights.description: Every exception frame in the live log stream is a clickable link that opens the corresponding Kotlin or Java source file at the exact line.

highlights.title: Auto-start on Android Run
highlights.description: The logcat stream starts automatically when Android Run launches the app and filters output to that process's PID from the first log line.

sections.heading: Features
bullets: Added a Logcat panel that streams ADB output from connected Android devices in a dedicated VS Code webview, removing the need to switch tools during development.
Stack traces in the live stream render as clickable deeplinks; selecting a frame navigates to the exact file and line in your source.
Logcat starts automatically when Android Run launches the app and follows its PID, so the panel shows only that app's output from the first moment.
A status bar pill reflects the current stream state and provides one-click access to start, stop, pause, resume, clear, and device switching.
A configurable ring buffer caps memory usage during long sessions; logs can be exported to a plain-text file for sharing or post-mortem analysis.
